The schema therefore only enforces/keeps `access_token`, and z.object's default 'strip' mode removes all other properties (expiry, refresh_token, instance_url, etc.). The code even relies on `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` which would have been stripped, confirming data loss. In credential-sync mode this means refreshed tokens lack expiry data, a real correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to model “any numeric property is expiry” and “allow other properties” via computed keys: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In a JS object literal these expressions are evaluated immediately, and `z.string()` is an object; calling `.toString()` produces a single literal property name (effectively `"[object Object]"`), and the second entry overwrites the first. The resulting Zod schema is essentially `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }` with Zod's default unknown-key behavior stripping all other keys. So in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), fields like `expiry_date` / `expires_in` / `instance_url` will be dropped even if present, leading to refreshed tokens missing expiry info (e.g., Office365/Zoom/Salesforce paths that call `parseRefreshTokenResponse`), which can keep credentials effectively expired.
